A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Frictional Q-Learning by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures, and tables, are readable and support comparison despite extensive revision.

before.justification: V1 Section 5 and Appendix B report original five-seed MuJoCo experiments, baseline comparisons, beta and augmentation ablations, and action-distribution histograms.

after.justification: V3 Section 5 reports original MuJoCo comparisons and additional fixed-buffer experiments involving FQL, BCQ, and FQL-V.

M1.justification: The written training procedure changes substantially. V3 Algorithm 1 feeds decoded actions into the actor/target actor and introduces an explicit reward-plus-discounted critic target. Section 4.4 replaces v1 Equation 13's ELBO maximization with minimization of Lt+Lb+TC. These are substantive specification changes, although inconsistent loss signs and latent-decoding descriptions leave implementation intent unresolved.

E1.justification: The same five MuJoCo-v4 environments are retained. V3 adds a distinct offline/imitation scenario using fixed buffers collected from suboptimal or moderate DDPG behavior policies, without further environment interaction. V1's reported experiments instead use evolving replay buffers.

E2.justification: DDPG, TD3, SAC, and MEow remain the online comparators. V3 Figure 4 newly evaluates BCQ in the fixed-buffer comparison and includes behavior-policy returns as a reference. This adds a substantive direct comparison against the batch-constrained method underlying FQL, which v1 discusses but does not experimentally compare.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a controlled fixed-buffer protocol using 1M transitions collected through noiseless DDPG rollouts and matched BCQ/FQL hyperparameters. Existing settings also change: Walker2D's critic learning rate changes from 1e-3 to 3e-4 and beta from 2 to 5; Hopper's cVAE learning rate changes from 1e-3 to 3e-4. These are revised reported settings, not merely additional disclosure.

E4.justification: V1's beta sweep, online Critic-versus-Augmentation comparison, and Appendix B.2 Humanoid action-distribution diagnostic are not retained. V3 instead studies complete-basis augmentation as FQL-V under fixed buffers, emphasizing early critic instability. The augmentation idea already existed, but its testing conditions and the broader supplementary evidence change substantially.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent seeds and standard deviations. Plot shading changes from standard deviation in v1 Figures 2–4 to explicitly labeled half-standard-deviation bands in v3 Figures 3–4. No increase in run counts or new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: All five FQL Step-style entries change, while corresponding online baseline entries remain numerically unchanged. For example, Humanoid is 6486.43 ± 144.90 in v1 Table 3 and 6726.52 ± 625.11 in v3 Table 1 under revised settings, so this is not an established same-setting gain. Seed and Final rows disappear. New fixed-buffer curves show task-dependent rankings, including BCQ ahead on Ant.

T1.justification: V1's reflection-symmetric heterogeneous-MDP argument and pi/4 angular bound are replaced by tangent/normal manifold geometry, directional-growth anisotropy, Lipschitz tolerances, and a local-isometry theorem. V3 Appendix A adds a projection-energy lemma and a restricted Bellman-operator convergence proof. The standard total-variation error bound is retained with an expanded derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from a frictional dual-buffer extension claiming convergence toward the true MDP to a geometric manifold framework with directional stability and local-isometry qualifications. V3 explicitly claims operation in both online off-policy and offline regimes and a first geometric interpretation of batch RL. The Walker2D/Humanoid performance claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 interprets fixed-buffer gains as geometric regularization independent of improved data collection and discusses augmentation's coverage/stability tradeoff. Its conclusion identifies unenforced encoder isometry as a limitation, replacing v1's emphasis on stochastic decoder instability. Appendix A.1 adds dimensionality-dependent qualifications to normal-direction dominance; earlier beta and low-dimensional-task interpretations are removed.

D1.justification: V3 adds minibatch latent-shuffling details for TC estimation, explicit storage of orthonormal basis sets, fixed-buffer collection instructions, and environment-specific cVAE table columns. Conversely, v1's runtime estimates, concurrent GPU seed execution, and 10,000-step evaluation cadence are omitted. Most shared architecture and optimizer details remain.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from a broad survey of physics-inspired RL toward support constraints, manifold geometry, isometric autoencoders, and Lipschitz analysis. V3 adds discussion of BEAR, BAIL, and related geometric work while removing much of the SVPG, diffusion, and continuous-time discussion. TD7 and RESeL are newly discussed but explicitly excluded from evaluation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, background, algorithm discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around geometry. New Analogy, Action Geometry, Affine Transformation, and Stability Bound subsections restructure the narrative. Results and proof appendices are reorganized; acknowledgments are removed and an Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: V3 changes the main text and references from one column to two, adds a manifold schematic and fixed-buffer plots, and redraws comparison curves with disclosed smoothing. The performance table moves into the main text with one summary row per algorithm. Earlier ablation and histogram displays disappear, and the hyperparameter tables gain columns.

improvement.justification: V3's direct fixed-buffer BCQ comparison addresses an important empirical omission, and its explicit isometry limitation improves transparency. However, removing beta sensitivity, distribution diagnostics, and numerical Seed/Final summaries weakens robustness evidence. V3 also leaves optimization signs and whether candidate decoding uses a zeroed nuisance latent or both latents inconsistent across Sections 4.4–4.5. These substantive benefits and unresolved losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
